name: Crystal Burbot
description: Crystal Burbot (Lota Crystallo) is a mystical fish that can be caught only at Christmas time. According to an old angling legend, this once voracious cold-blooded predator was turned to crystalline form by the Ice Queen for eating her magic white mice. And while this version might sound like childish nonsense, no one has yet come up with a better explanation for the existence of a crystal-bodied fish. Go figure.

name: Dingonek
description: The Dingonek is a massive creature, weighing up to 155 kg (340 lbs), with a head resembling a lioness marked like a leopard, and two long white fangs protruding from its upper jaw. Its broad back, covered in armadillo-like scales, is reminiscent of a hippo's. A wide, finned tail allows it to stay afloat in swift currents. Some believe it may be a descendant of prehistoric reptiles that survived in remote regions, though no bones or skin samples have been found. Eyewitness accounts, however, leave little room for doubt about its existence.

name: Double Head Eel
description: The Double Head Eel (Anguilla Bicephalus) is a terror of the depths that frightens even the most experienced anglers. This mutated predator, weighing up to 35 kg (77 lbs), has two fully functional heads, each with its own mind and an insatiable hunger for hunting. Its snake-like body is covered in slime that releases toxins, paralyzing its prey upon contact. The Double Head Eel can attack from both sides simultaneously, making it nearly unbeatable in close combat. It breaks through underwater obstacles and attacks from unexpected angles. It is said that its appearance is always accompanied by electrical storms, as if nature itself is warning of the danger.

name: Fierce Muskie
description: Hiding in underwater thickets and under snags, this burning Monster tirelessly seeks out new defenseless victims. The spirit of fire endowed it with unbridled malice and unquenchable bloodthirstiness.

name: Fire Muskie
description: The otherworldly spirits endowed this disgusting creature with exorbitant gluttony. This Muskie devastates reservoirs, gobbling up all the fish clean. Its glowing, fiery body glides through underwater vegetation, leaving no chance for survival for anyone.

name: Frankenfish
description: Frankenfish (Monstrum Ichtiandras) - a bizarre result of an originally innocent prank gone wrong, this infernal abomination was sewn together from different fish parts by a fisherman’s son to give his angling friends a good fright on Halloween. On that dark and stormy night, just as the boy prepared to pull the monstrosity out of the water and terrify his pals, a bolt of lightning struck the water and the gruesome creature miraculously came to life! With a powerful jerk the monster pulled our unexpecting prankster into the dark water abyss...

name: Furry Trout
description: Furry Trout (Oncorhynchus Furrycus) this legendary fish belongs to the Trout family and is believed to be a nonexistent hoax by most anglers. Legend has it, that the Furry Trout is more ferocious than the Himalayan Yeti, more ruthless than the Loch Ness Monster! And yet...the white furry floof is actually cute as hell! Similar in size and appearance to its direct relative, the Rainbow Trout, Furry Trout is the result of evolutionary metamorphosis. The poor thing had to grow thick fluffy fur in order to keep itself warm and survive in the severe cold waters of its harsh northern environment. Aww...

name: Ghost Pike
description: Ghost Pike (Esox Spiritus). Wow! Looks like you’re terribly in luck! You managed to catch the mysterious Ghost Pike - a rare anomaly that’s been spotted in many of America’s waterways this Halloween. Some find it terrifyingly mystical, others tend to believe there’s simple radiation involved. Whatever the case may be, this monster Pike is glowing like a real ghost and now you can tell everyone about catching one!

name: Grass Carp-Ghost
description: Evil spirits have possessed a large specimen of the Grass Carp. Now this creature is devouring all aquatic vegetation of the reservoir, threatening its ecological balance.

name: Green Ogre Gar
description: Green Ogre Gar is a true Monster menace that roams the quiet waters of Neherrin at night around Halloween. Weighing around 11-15 kg (24-34 lb), this is one tough mutant to catch. But oh boy, are you in for some excitement while trying.

name: Hellish Muskie
description: A huge fish glowing with a fiery haze has appeared in the reservoir, eating everyone smaller than itself. This abomination entered our world on Halloween, when the fabric of reality between the worlds became very thin. And it looks like this creature is not in a hurry to leave.

name: Hybrid Carp-Ghost
description: At first glance, this fish looks like a particularly large Hybrid Carp, but the ghostly light emanating from its translucent body indicates otherwise.

name: Largemouth Bass-Phantom
description: On Halloween, these predatory fish turned into glowing monsters and took over the whole reservoir, terrorizing its inhabitants. It is said that flickering lights can be spotted over the water surface where they live.

name: Leather Carp-Ghost
description: You would never have seen this possessed Carp if not for the otherworldly gates that opened on Halloween. Now this creature has intimidated the inhabitants of the reservoir so much that they are scared to move and find some food.

name: Leprechaun Fish
description: Leprechaun Fish (Leprechaunus Ichtiandrus) - a small fish, shamrock green in color that is by some believed to be a myth. But every year on St. Patrick’s Day there are reports of a very fishy anomaly. Legend has it, that long ago one very hungry Green Sunfish found the leprechaun’s pot of gold at the end of the rainbow and...ate it! So if you engage in a fierce fish fight with what seems to be a monster the size of a Trophy Catfish...don’t be too stunned to land an adversary no bigger than your typical sunfish! True or not, believe it or not, but you should definitely try your luck at catching the Leprechaun Fish.

name: Mirror Carp-Ghost
description: This massive Mirror Carp has become a receptacle for evil spirits that have broken into our world through otherworldly gates. Now this translucent ghostly voracious creature is depriving the inhabitants of the reservoir of their food.

name: Northern Snakehead
description: Northern Snakehead ( Channa argus ) is a slick and agile thing, that looks like a real snake! The homeland of Snakehead is the rivers of the Far Eastern region. However today this sly one made its way into many reservoirs of Europe and America. And this is completely not good at all, because Snakehead belongs to the invasive species of predators. It grows quickly, quickly breeds, and quickly devours everything it can devour, including other fish, tadpoles, frogs, and even birds! Just imagine, this thing can live up to 5 days without water, burrowing in the silt, and is able to move on land in search of a new plentiful pond. With such appetites, it is not surprising that it can grow more than a meter in length and gain about 10 kg (22 lb) of weight. Usually it hides under snags and in waterplants in shallow water, preferring heavily overgrown areas. Help us all St. Patrick! If you don't stop this villain, the entire fauna of the reservoir will suffer!

name: Prussian Carp-Ghost
description: The pale light emitted by these creatures can hardly dispel the darkness of the depths of the other world that has disgorged these creatures. They glide in the water silently, scaring away the inhabitants of the reservoirs with their unnatural ghostly light.

name: Rowdy Bass
description: Rowdy Bass (Micropterus Debaucherous) Yeehaw! This is one tough barbaric beast to ride! The Rowdy Bass is such a rare occurrence in these waters, that only few are actually said to have seen them around St.Patrick’s Day. Hard to find and even harder to catch, given you’re lucky enough to land one on your hook, these debaucherous monsters will give you the fish fight of your life! And no wonder, the feisty character is in this fiery fish’s blood.

name: Slide Rock Bolter
description: The Slide-Rock Bolter (Macrostoma saxiperrumptus) is a bizarre and fearsome creature recounted by the lumberjacks of North America during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is believed to live in the mountains of Colorado. The creature has an immense head, small eyes, and a large mouth, weighing up to 160 kg (350 lbs). Its tail ends in a fluke similar to a dolphin, equipped with enormous grab-hooks. This fearsome animal uses the grab-hooks on its split tail to latch onto the crest of a mountain or ridge. Once it spots its prey, it lifts its tail to release its hold, then slides down, scooping its victims into its mouth. When not hunting, the Bolter resides in the depths of mountain lakes.

name: Smallmouth Bass-Phantom
description: The breath of the other world has changed the once ordinary predators. Now these glowing creatures have taken over the reservoir and are pestering its inhabitants. It is said that flickering lights can be spotted over the water surface where they live.

name: Steelhead-Phantom
description: An otherworldly glow emanates from within these creatures and instills mystical fear in everyone around. There are legends that Jack himself — yes, THAT Jack — was very fond of snacking on Salmons like this one.

name: Sturgeon-Demon
description: A demon has entered the otherworldly gates and possessed this Sturgeon, distorting it beyond recognition! Red-brown scales, vertical pupils, and forward-pointing horns — a truly chilling sight!

name: Tarpon-Demon
description: This otherworldly abomination hardly resembles a Tarpon anymore. Its blood-red color, infernal vertical pupils, and curved horns label it as a demon that has crossed into our world through the thinned fabric of reality.

name: Trout-Ghost
description: Exuding ghostly light, these creatures from the other world intimidate the whole reservoir. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

name: Trout-Phantom
description: This beautiful rainbow trout has been transformed into a terrible creature, glowing with otherworldly light and indiscriminately devouring all underwater dwellers. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

name: Trout-Skeleton
description: Only the otherworldly forces could bring such monsters to life! These skeletons once belonged to common Trouts, but they have now come to life to instill fear in the underwater dwellers. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

name: Vampire Biara
description: Vampire Biara (Rhaphiodon vulpinus vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish, weighing up to 60 kg (132 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Biara feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

name: Historic Black Crappie
description: Historic Black Crappie (Pomoxis Nigromaculatus) is a really fishy piece of history! This particular specimen bears a special anchor tag on its fin is marked with the year 1796 and engraved with President’s George Washington’s signature! Apparently, that very year a number of fish hatchlings were released on July 4th to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Indeed, a truly historic specimen!

Such cases of long-lifers among these historic fish are rare, but not entirely unknown to scientists, who have been trying in vain to solve this mystery for many years...

That day, on 4th July 1796, many young fish were released with anchors tags bearing President’s George Washington’s signature to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence.

Just imagine, this Chinook is over 200 years old! Judging by the anchor tag clipped onto its fin, this very fish had been tagged and released into these waters along with many other hatchlings on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Talk about capturing a piece of history!

How it lived up to this day - remains a mystery that might never be solved!

But this particular Muskie is beyond old - judging by the anchor tag clipped onto its fin, it's one of the many young fish released into these waters over 200 years ago to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence! No doubt about it - the tag bears the release date and President George Washington's signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history! Long live the Muskie king!

name: Historic Rainbow Trout
description: Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus Mykiss) are predatory fish with a very diverse diet. Neither mouse nor fish stand a chance if spotted by this hungry carnivore. Perhaps such a healthy appetite made it possible for this particular specimen to live over 200 years! No kidding, this very Rainbow Trout is one of the special hatchlings that were tagged with a special ring bearing President’s George Washington’s signature and released on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence.

name: Historic Smallmouth Bass
description: Smallmouth Bass (Micropterus Dolomieu) is perhaps one of the most popular game fish among anglers in North America. You’ve probably caught hundreds of these fish. But this time you’re in for a real surprise! When still just a hatchling, this very Smallmouth was released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. description: Striped Bass (Morone saxatilis) is generally a very resilient and die-hard fish. Known to tolerate both salt and fresh water, the oldest Striper ever recorded was 31 years of age. But looks like the specimen you just caught is way beyond anything in the book of World Records - this particular fish is over 200 years old! As unbelievable as it may be - there can be no doubt if you examine the anchor tag with President George Washington’s signature. It means that this Striper was one of the many young fish released into these waters on 4th July 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Talk about luck!

There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin bears the engraved year and President George Washington’s initials!

description: White Crappie (Pomoxis Annularis) are widespread panfish in North America with a relatively short lifespan. But you managed to catch an extremely rare specimen! This very White Crappie comes from the pool of young fish that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history! The only question that remains a mystery is how this White Crappie manage to live such a long life...?

name: Blue Bandit Aracu
description: Okay, so you arrive at your fishing spot and see a bearded bandit looking at you from the water depth. What would you do? Why, catch the rascal and make him lead you to his boss – Crumbling Krampus Payara! This is how you can return the beard back to Santa and save Christmas. By the way, rumor has it that the Bandit Aracu is extremely fond of donuts.

name: Blue Dunce Crappie
description: Some think that glasses make you look smarter. But it doesn’t work if you are a dunce, such as this Crappie! He helped the Unlucky Krampus Tarpon to steal Santa’s glasses. And he is not sorry for doing it. Teach him a good lesson, and also find out where his boss is hiding. To catch more Crappies, make sure to stock up on cookies and milk. It’s their favorite snack!

name: Blue Foolish Goby
description: What would you call a Goby, who helped to steal a precious item of headwear from Santa? Now the Clumsy Krampus Eel has the hat, and it won’t be easy to find the villain without his Goby accomplice. But if you have some cookies, your chances to catch the troublemaker increase. So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

name: Clumsy Krampus Eel
description: What was this Clumsy Krampus Eel thinking, stealing Santa’s hat? Did he honestly want to deliver presents in a reindeer sleigh? Most likely he just had one too many drinks with his old mischievous Krampus pals, enjoying the party punch a bit too enthusiastically. But this character is not as simple as he looks. It will take some effort to get the hat back! However, we know for sure that the elderly Eel has a very sweet tooth and can’t resist a Christmas treat, such as cakes or stollen.

name: Crumbling Krampus Payara
description: Just look at this Crumbling Krampus Payara – she would gladly use her set of false teeth to snatch away anything that doesn’t belong to her. Who can tell why she would need Santa’s Beard? It’s plainly obvious that this fish is just an obnoxious old relic, tipsy on eggnog! No choice but to get some candy to catch the thief and make her give the Beard back, because Santa surely needs it!

name: Decorated Alligator Gar
description: Alligator Gars (Atractosteus spatula) are among the largest freshwater fish in North America. They are found in the southern regions of the United States extending down to Mexico and inhabit primarily large, slow-moving rivers, freshwater lakes, swamps, estuaries, and bays. These fish can breathe both air and water and bear a resemblance to American alligators, having torpedo-shaped bodies armored with nearly impenetrable scales and broad snouts with long sharp teeth. description: Silver Carp (Hypophthalmichthys Molitrix) is a large freshwater fish of the Carp family native to East Asian rivers. These schooling fish primarily inhabit large rivers. Silver Carp have elongated bodies with gray-greenish backs, silvery sides, and underbelly. They are easily distinguished from other fish of the Carp family by their unusually low position of the eyes and large size. And what’s that? It looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

name: Decorated Tiger Muskie
description: Tiger Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy × lucius), commonly called Tiger Muskie, is a hybrid of the Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) and the Northern Pike (Esox lucius). This carnivorous fish lives in freshwater lakes and rivers ranging from Canada, the Northeast, and to the Midwest United States. These fish grow stronger and faster than their parent fish and are quite a challenge to catch, therefore even called “Fish of 10,000 casts”. Tiger Muskies have vertical stripes on a light background, which is the opposite color scheme of a Northern Pike. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

name: Decorated White Crappie
description: White Crappie (Pomoxis annularis) is a freshwater fish native to North America, that was successfully introduced to many other countries. This species is typically found in warm murky (turbid) rivers and lakes. Its body is silvery in color with dark lateral bars along its side and a white belly. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what ...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

name: Decorated White Sturgeon
description: White Sturgeon (Acipenser Transmontanus), is a species of Sturgeon that is the largest freshwater fish in North America. These fish live on the bottoms of slow-moving rivers, bays, and estuarine areas along the west coast of North America from the Aleutian Islands to Central California. White Sturgeon have slender bodies, usually ranging in colour from greenish gray to light gray. These fish have no scales and are covered in armor of large bony plates. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

name: Decorated Zander
description: Zander (Sander Lucioperca) is a popular European game species of fish that is closely related to Perch and is often called the European Pikeperch. Although widespread in both freshwater and brackish habitats throughout western Eurasia, Zander prefer to inhabit large freshwater rivers and lakes. Sometimes called Pike-perch, Zander is even considered to be a hybrid of the two species, as it looks a lot like Pike due to its elongated body, while having a spiny dorsal fin, just like Perch. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

name: Green Bandit Aracu
description: Okay, so you arrive at your fishing spot and see a bearded bandit looking at you from the water depth. What would you do? Why, catch the rascal and make him lead you to his boss – Crumbling Krampus Payara! This is how you can return the beard back to Santa and save Christmas. By the way, rumor has it that the Bandit Aracu is extremely fond of donuts.

name: Green Dunce Crappie
description: Some think that glasses make you look smarter. But it doesn’t work if you are a dunce, such as this Crappie! He helped the Unlucky Krampus Tarpon to steal Santa’s glasses. And he is not sorry for doing it. Teach him a good lesson, and also find out where his boss is hiding. To catch more Crappies, make sure to stock up on cookies and milk. It’s their favorite snack!

name: Green Foolish Goby
description: What would you call a Goby, who helped to steal a precious item of headwear from Santa? Now the Clumsy Krampus Eel has the hat, and it won’t be easy to find the villain without his Goby accomplice. But if you have some cookies, your chances to catch the troublemaker increase. So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

name: Unlucky Krampus Tarpon
description: This old Tarpon has clearly had a bit too much eggnog. He’s not quite as menacing as in the days of old, but there is still fight left in him! At the very least, he was capable enough to nick Santa’ glasses. Alas, he forgot to give them back, which is not surprising, given his age. It would be a good idea to find the old guy and gently remind him that Santa needs his glasses more. The problem is, the Unlucky Tarpon has long since lost his lower jaw. Well, you’ll just have to use this special lure...

name: Albino Blackfish
description: Albino Blackfish (Dallia Albineus) infected by radiation from a toxic waste leak, these specimen of otherwise black Alaska Blackfish are absolutely white in color and seem to have a particularly insatiable craving for Salmon eggs. Although these infected fish are hardly over 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) in weight, they are rather numerous and therefore present a serious problem causing much damage to the populations of Salmon species.

name: Black Whisker
description: Black Whisker (Silurus Nigreos) - this huge whiskered monster has devoured so much fish in Sander Baggersee Lake, that its belly and eyes look like they are about to burst! Even so, the Black Whisker doesn't plan to stop its feeding frenzy, thus putting the lake’s entire ecosystem at risk. Not unless some fearless angler puts an end to this dark foodsie’s nightmare!

name: Carp Colossus
description: Colossus Carp (Cyprinidae Colossus) - a Carp unlike any you’ve ever seen, this colossal monstrous creature is terrorizing the peaceful waters of Weeping Willow fisheries! Even the largest trophy-sized species are terrified of this fat-bellied underwater titan, lurking in the murky depths. Will anyone find a way to lure the Colossus Carp out of its underwater lair?

name: Cyber Piranha
description: Piranhas are cautious and even shy, but Cyber Piranhas are completely devoid of natural behavior. These monsters are modified with various implants that make them incredibly dangerous. A mechanically strengthened body, cybernetic vision, sharp adamant-covered teeth, and the instincts of real schooling predators — this is exactly what terminator fish look like! But for every terminator, there is a melting furnace — or, in this case, an Electrical Leader.

name: Dendrofin
description: Dendrofin (Amia Dendronimus) this extremely fishy mutation of what used to be your ordinary Bowfin is the result of an ambush predator going vegan! After all, you are what you eat! Or so they say. At least, the Dendrofin would agree. Looks like this particular specimen swapped his ordinary carnivorous diet for genuine tree bark and now miraculously resembles an old log! Gotta hand it to the vegan diet - this powerful monster has grown to nearly 6 kg (13 lb) and is getting stronger by the day! Who cares how you look when you’re that big, right? But while sporting such a tree-like texture might be Dendrofin’s great camouflage, we sure know what kind of bait this wood-hungry monster won’t resist!

name: Eel Cannibal
description: Cannibal Eel (Anguilla Canibalium) was smuggled into the peaceful waters of Ghent-Terneuzen canal from Africa by rebellious trouble-makers. It looks horrifying enough to scare any angler out of their wits. This monster seems to have a particular taste for its own kind, heartlessly hunting for other Eels and decimating their population!

name: Eldergar
description: Eldergar (Lepisosteus Antiquus) is probably the oldest known Longnose Gar ever recorded. Having well outlived the typical lifespan of its own species, the Eldergar at least 70 years old, which is twice the age of the oldest specimen previously recorded! No wonder this old-timer is also the largest Longnose in history - weighing almost 25 kg (55 lb)! Ichthyologists believe the reason behind this anomaly to be found in the Eldergar’s feeding habits. It appears that this old-timer has taken to a very strange diet: not only does the Eldergar hunt exclusively on American Shad, but seems to be feeding entirely of their heads, leaving the rest of the Shad bodies to be eaten by scavengers.

name: Elusive Arapaima
description: This is probably the oldest and most cunning Arapaima you can ever encounter. The local legends say that this monster is the evil spirit of Lake Maku-Maku, who has lived there since time immemorial. Anyone who tried to catch it failed at best, and at worst — disappeared altogether! They say neither tridents, nor nets, nor strong tackle can take it on. However, there is a way for a brave angler to land this ancient fish!

name: Fenrivore
description: Legends say the Fenrivore was born from the cursed blood of Fenrir, the giant wolf fated to devour Odin at Ragnarök. When his blood spilled into the ocean during a fierce battle, the sea twisted the curse into flesh, shaping creatures with wide maws and wolf-sharp teeth. Drawn together by that same dark hunger, the Fenrivores hunt in packs, striking swiftly to claim as many victims as the deep will offer. To this day, local anglers whisper that these horrors are the ocean’s omen of Ragnarök.

name: Fighter Shark
description: Young sharks are known to often become prey to local caimans. However, this particular monster has won many battles with the sharp-toothed reptiles. Its hundreds of scars and the only remaining eye speak eloquently about its victories. Having gained strength and experience, the monster itself became a menace to the caimans, which are worshiped by the local tribe!

name: Ghost Peacock Bass
description: Ghost Peacock Bass (Cichla Exspiravit) - this pale, red-eyed monster seems to stir quite a panic among all other fish, making it impossible for anglers to enjoy their favorite pastime at this waterway! Seen only at night, the Ghost Peacock Bass will turn anyone who catches it into a real ghostbusting hero in the eyes of the local angling community!

name: Gourmet Bass
description: Gourmet Bass (Morone Gurmanius) this huge specimen is way over the size of any freshwater Bass you could hope to catch! Weighing roughly 30 kg (75 lb), the Gourmet Bass gets its size and name from its highly gourmet dietary habits. Apparently, it developed quite a taste for nutritious, protein-rich foods and will eat any molluscs it can find!

name: Grayling Wrestler
description: Grayling Wrestler (Thymallus Luctator) is a monstrous type of European Grayling with a temper so malicious that it has turned its color to dark, almost black! It’ll take some wits and skills to catch this mad fighter!

name: Grouperzilla
description: Grouperzilla is a creature born from the depths of the polluted oceans, where an ordinary huge grouper transformed into a giant sea monster. It’s known for its considerable size and strength, far exceeding any known representative of its species. Grouperzilla is known for its aggressive behavior and insatiable appetite. It often hunts for its favorite snack — lobsters — and can attack the boats of anglers who have this delicacy on board.

name: Helgaflut
description: Once upon a time, Odin punished the people for their greed, sending a harsh winter that emptied the sea and brought hunger to the villages. However, his wife Frigg, moved by pity for the families and their children, wept into the empty waters, turning her tears into Helgaflut. With a sacred fire in their hearts, these fish melted the ice and saved the people of Isvikheimen from hungry death. From that day on, every angler who catches Helgafllut is granted a year of good fortune and full keepnets.

name: Hordecuda
description: The sunlit atolls of the Maldives have been thrown into chaos by a terrifying phenomenon — the Horde of Barracudas. Typically, adult Barracudas are solitary hunters, but now they have united into a relentless, predatory gang. This wild horde tears through the reefs, leaving nothing but destruction and panic in its wake. Moving with uncanny coordination, they hunt as one, instantly surrounding their prey and giving it no chance to escape. A Horde of Barracudas isn't just a danger — it's a force of nature. In the Maldives, they are known as the Hordecuda.

name: Mad-Eye Buffalo
description: Mad-Eye Buffalo (Ictiobus Oculus) Considered to be a figment of some anglers’ imagination, the Mad-Eye Buffalo is nevertheless very real and is in fact a rare and extremely strange mutation of the freshwater Smallmouth Buffalo. This monstrous fish gets its name for having magically sharp eyesight that, legend has it, allows it to see through anything - from walls to the human soul. It can also spot the most intricate details in any light, which means, that catching this monster will require using some of the thinnest and frailest fishing like you can find! Quite a challenge, considering that the Mad-Eye weighs around 6 kg (13 lb)!

name: Mega Piranha
description: Nobody knows whose evil genius combined the most voracious fish in South America with the latest achievements in biomechatronics to create incredibly powerful cyborg monsters! Razor-sharp teeth made from solid adamant, improved bodies with mechanical fins, cyber vision, and inherent bloodthirstiness — what else do ideal killer fish need? To tackle one of these monstrosities, you’ll need a miracle — or an Adamant Leader!

name: Mighty M'Benga
description: Local legends say that the Congo is home to an evil spirit named M'Benga, which can possess river dwellers. It seems that this spirit has inhabited a particularly large specimen of Goliath Tigerfish. The spirit grants the monster fish demonic strength and bloodthirstiness. According to the legend, only the blood of its fellow species and a special ritual performed by a real shaman can temporarily calm the fury of M'Benga. So hurry up — you don't have much time!

name: Muskie Golem
description: Muskie Golem (Esox Stonius) - there are many fish legends among the anglers of Saint Croix Lake, one of which is about the Muskie Golem. This fish gets its name for having abnormally large and tough scales that make it look as if made of rock. The Muskie Golem is also said to be well over a hundred years old and weighs almost 35 kg (75 lb), which makes it the largest Muskie specimen in all of Saint Croix! Virtually uncatchable, as it seems to take no interest in any typical baits or lures.

name: Night Windrazor
description: In the tropical waters of the Maldives, where moonlight glides over the waves, sailors whisper of the Night Razor — a legendary Sailfish Monster. This sleek predator moves between lagoons in a heartbeat, leaving behind only a sharp, silvery flash. Some mistake it for moonlight, but seasoned fishermen know the truth — when you see that flash, the Night Razor is hunting. Unlike ordinary Sailfish, this one hides in the deep to stalk Luminous Flying Fish that stand out even at night. Night Razor's ruthless hunting style and raw strength make it a formidable challenge to catch.

name: Perch Bully
description: Perch Bully (Perca Corruptor) is a ferocious predator unlike any Perch you’ve ever seen! Relentlessly hunting down its prey and devouring any fish it can bite into with its big mouth and razor sharp teeth, the Perch Bully can only be caught using a special type of lure!

name: Pikeslasher
description: Pikeslasher (Sander Murderus) a genuine mystery to ichthyologists, the Pikeslasher is a blood-thirsty mutation of the common Walleye that has developed quite a taste for Pike! Who knows, perhaps this is a fishy case of personal vendetta, a thrilling story of Walleye vengeance for a loved one that was heartlessly, yet naturally, consumed by Pike sometime in the past... We’ll probably never know the Pikeslasher’s true motives. But what we do know, is that this gigantic carnivorous monster has adopted the coloration of a Pike and now weighs about 10 kg (22 lb)! Looks like you’ll need to make some first rate pike cutbait to trick the Pikeslasher into biting.

name: Rainbow Outlaw
description: Rainbow Outlaw (Oncorhynchus Genetikus) this abnormally large specimen of a lake form Rainbow Trout was apparently sneaky enough to escape from one of Oregon’s trout farms, where it was genetically engineered to grow extra-large. The oversized runaway resorted to some meticulous route planning to make its escape - using a network of underground streams it traveled between different lakes until settling down in Falcon’s peaceful waters. But while this genetically modified organism succeeded in covering its tracks from the fish farmers, it’s huge size of over 25 kg (50 lb) is a dead giveaway. And feeding exclusively on Brown Trout Eggs, the Rainbow Outlaw is only getting bigger.

name: Striped Blade
description: The Striped Blade Monster is an incredible Marlin known for its speed and aggressiveness. Its long, sword-like snout is supernaturally tough, allowing it to cut through even the strongest fishing nets. The iridescent stripes on this Monster’s body serve as a warning sign in the underwater environment, clearly indicating who’s in charge here. These stripes also emit a faint glow, which creates the impression of dancing light in the dark depths of the ocean and attracts underwater creatures. This graceful and powerful monster will become the jewel of any sophisticated collection.

name: Sturgeon Leviathan
description:
Leviathan Sturgeon (Acipenseridae Pristis) is a huge monster fish found in the Dnipro River. Known for its impressive size and strength, this fish is a dream catch for adventurous anglers looking for a thrilling challenge. To reel in this unique giant, you'll need a combination of skill, a bit of luck, and some special lures.

Cookies and Mussels Groundbait

name: Taimen-Khan
description: This huge Taimen has no competitors because of its impressive size. This is an excellent hunter who is constantly on the move. This Taimen is not too picky in terms of food: it’s happy to eat rodents and waterfowl that have fallen into the water as well as small fish. According to old-timers, it once used to drag dogs into the deep. This specimen is rightfully considered the Khan of the entire Selenge River.

name: Terror Tarpon
description: Terror Tarpon (Megalops Terroristus) looking scarred and hostile, this highly aggressive Tarpon came to the quiet marshy areas of the Everglades from the brackish coastal prairies and is terrorizing the local fish. Although relatively average in size, weighing just about 20 kg (44 lb), this feisty trouble maker is doing a lot of damage to the underwater ecosystem of this area by seriously diminishing the population of Largemouth Bass, which it seems to have a particular taste for.

name: Thorn-Ripper
description: The Thorn-Ripper is an aggressive monster fish that lives in the depths of the Dnipro River. Its spikes grew over centuries of survival among predators, serving as both defense and weapon. Legends say that humans once fished out its family, and since then, the Thorn-Ripper has been seeking revenge on fishermen by piercing boats with its spikes. When it hears the sound of a boat above its territory, it swiftly attacks, puncturing it like needles. Fishermen now fear encountering this underwater menace. Since this fish is extremely cautious, only a unique lure like the Wasp Walker can capture its interest.

name: Tyrannotrout
description: Tyrannotrout (Oncorhynchus Tyrannosaurus) a.k.a the T-Rex Trout, is a carnivorous prehistoric monster of the Salmon family that has inexplicably infested the waters of one of New York’s most calm and peaceful lakes! Being a fairly small fish of under 1 kg (2.2 lb), a single T-Rex Trout couldn’t do much harm. Except from, maybe, biting your hand off. However, these razor-toothed flesh-hungry monsters hunt in schools and are endangering the entire population of fish in Rocky Lake! As there’s plenty of easy prey for these beasts to devour, the only way to get a Tyrannotrout’s attention is by using a special turtle-shell prehistoric lure.

name: Voodoo Fish
description: Voodoo Fish (Lota Magicus) according to an old indian legend, this mythical fish belongs to an extinct species that possessed magical powers and was a distant ancestor of today’s Burbot. Apparently the last remaining specimen of its kind, this age-old monster dwells in an abysmal hole somewhere in the deepest part of White Moose Lake and comes out to roam closer to the lake’s surface every once in a blue moon! No one knows exactly how long this archaic creature has lived for, but judging from the ancient markings of Northern indigenous tribes on its back, the Voodoo Fish was a part of some magical rituals that date back to over a century!

name: Wailing Catfish
description: This huge and greedy catfish was nicknamed Wailing for a reason. The low sounds emitted by this giant resemble underwater growling and can be heard hundreds of yards away from the Marron River. Its cries spreading through the jungle can scare not only fish and animals, but also people. And although it’s known for certain that some catfish can make loud sounds, no ichthyologists have ever heard such a roar. Rest assured, they would give a lot to get their hands on such a specimen!

name: Zombie Cat
description: Zombie Cat (Mortuus Consumus) while all Catfish are bottom-feeding scavengers in general, and among other things may consume dead fish, this particular whiskery monster has taken such an uncomely diet to the extreme. Gravely and old, the Zombie Cat feeds exclusively on any rotten and decaying organisms it can find on the bottom of swampy Quanchkin Lake. Looking rather like a monster from a Pet Cemetery horror sequel, this consumer of death is spreading a putrid smell all around the area!
